newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian president vetoes bill on UES ownership.
newsitem.headline: Russian president vetoes bill on UES ownership.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin has vetoed a bill passed on Friday by the lower house of parliament limiting foreign ownership in national power utility RAO UES to 25 percent, the president's press service said.
The Kremlin said Yeltsin had vetoed the law, which also requires the state maintain a 51 percent stake in the company, on Thursday -- before it was passed by the State Duma.
The Russian Constitution provides for presidential consideration of a bill only after it has been passed by both chambers of parliament.
The UES bill has only passed the lower house in the three readings required.
An aide to the Duma industrial policy committee said the Duma would send the bill on to the upper chamber Federation Council in any case.
The state currently owns a little over 52 percent of the company, UES officials said last month.
UES owns the national power grid, has controlling stakes in most regional power utilities and has stakes in a number of generating plants.
The government is mulling reforming the energy structure, and newly appointed First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov has said prices must go down in the sector.
At 1150 GMT, shares in RAO Yedinaya Energeticheskaya Sistema Rossii (UES) had fallen to $0.1845 from $0.1910 on the Russian Trading System.
